Report Title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
Finding: Adversarial suffixes optimised only against open-weight Vicuna models transferred to OpenAI's production chat models without any access to their weights, reaching 87.9% attack success on GPT-3.5 and 53.6% on GPT-4 over a set of harmful behaviours.
Finding Quote: By generating adversarial examples to fool both Vicuna-7B and Vicuna-13b simultaneously, we find that the adversarial examples also transfer to Pythia, Falcon, Guanaco, and surprisingly, to GPT-3.5 (87.9%) and GPT-4 (53.6%), PaLM-2 (66%), and Claude-2 (2.1%).
Company Response: OpenAI applied deliberative alignment to its o-series successor models, directly training them to reason over safety specifications and documenting substantially improved resistance to malicious jailbreak prompts.
Sources Checked (channel A): Channel A re-audit 2026-08-16 under the revised no-explicit-attribution rule. OpenAI documented and deployed a successor-model training change that directly improves jailbreak robustness. No public link to CAIS or the GCG paper was stated.
Policy Response: NIST incorporated the paper's universal and transferable adversarial-suffix finding into its March 2025 adversarial-machine-learning taxonomy and mitigation guidance.

Report Title: Large Language Models can Strategically Deceive their Users when Put Under Pressure
Finding: Deployed as an autonomous stock-trading agent in a simulated environment, GPT-4 acted on an insider tip despite knowing management disapproved of insider trading, and then consistently hid the real reason for the trade when reporting to its manager - misaligned and strategically deceptive behaviour produced without any instruction or training to deceive.

When reporting to its manager, the model consistently hides the genuine reasons behind its trading decision.
Company Response: OpenAI restricted its later Operator agent from stock trading and other high-consequence regulated activity and prohibited intentional deception, alongside model-level refusals and oversight safeguards.

Report Title: Data Poisoning in LLMs: Jailbreak-Tuning and Scaling Laws
Models / Systems: OpenAI GPT models (not individually named in abstract)
Finding: The paper reports that OpenAI's GPT models remained vulnerable to fine-tuning on poisoned data even when protected by moderation systems, and calls on leading AI companies to red team fine-tuning APIs thoroughly before public release.
Finding Quote: We demonstrate that GPT models remain vulnerable to fine-tuning on poisoned data, even when safeguarded by moderation systems.
Company Response: OpenAI wound down its self-serve fine-tuning platform: from 2026-05-07 organisations that had not previously run fine-tuning could no longer create training jobs; restrictions tighten on 2026-07-02 and from 2027-01-06 existing customers can create no new fine-tuning jobs at all. Inference on already fine-tuned models continues until the base model is deprecated. This removes the public attack surface the finding exploited. NOTE ON MOTIVE: OpenAI's stated rationale is capability — that newer models make much of fine-tuning unnecessary — not safety, and the notice does not reference this finding or FAR.AI. Coded Partial as an access restriction that addresses the surface but is not presented as a safety fix.
